subject.title: feat: enable the new exec approvals pipeline behind an opt-in setting

question: Should this default-off exec-approvals rollout merge without a successful real gateway/MXC proof, given that the available live proof ran with the sandbox disabled and the prompt UI is not yet wired?
rationale: The implementation appears internally sound, but only maintainers can accept the residual command-execution boundary risk or require the repository-mandated MXC proof before enabling an operator-accessible preview path.

options.title: Require MXC proof
options.body: Hold the PR until a capable host proves allowed execution and blocked sandbox access through the real gateway and Windows node path.

options.title: Accept preview risk
options.body: Merge the default-off hidden setting based on the existing MCP proof while explicitly owning the missing MXC validation as a preview limitation.

options.title: Pause until rollout UX
options.body: Defer production wiring until the prompt UI and a supported settings surface define a complete operator rollout contract.

recommendation.title: Require MXC proof
recommendation.body: Hold the PR until a capable host proves allowed execution and blocked sandbox access through the real gateway and Windows node path.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged history ties this person to the existing `system.run` security and execution policy that the new path would supplement.
